title: Neurophysiological Changes associated with Treatment of Depression in Youth
summary:
This study investigates whether brain signals measured using EEG can help determine the severity of depression in adolescents and predict treatment outcomes. It also examines how the ability to recognize emotions in faces changes during inpatient treatment.
The study includes three sessions (T0–T2):
At the first session (T0), parents and children receive detailed information about the study and complete questionnaires.
At the second session (T1), the child performs an emotion recognition task while brain activity (EEG) and eye movements (eye tracking) are recorded.
After this, the child undergoes standard clinical treatment for approximately six weeks.
At the final session (T2), the same measurements are repeated to assess changes following treatment.

interventions.name: Adolescents with depressive symptoms presenting for their first clinical referral will undergo EEG and eye-tracking assessments while performing an emotional recognition task. The same measurements will be repeated after six weeks of standard clinical treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age between 11 and 17 years 
• A confirmed diagnosis of depression; there must be no comorbid diagnosis of a neuropsychiatric developmental disorder, such as autism or ADHD
• An IQ of at least average
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute suicidal ideation
• Use of benzodiazepines
• Current or past neurological disorders
• Insufficient knowledge of German

Additional exclusion criteria for eye tracking
• Nystagmus
• Strabismus
• Uncorrected visual impairment
• Use of stimulants
• Use of sedatives
